# From RFQ to bid

**Turn a public tender into a correct, signed bid without a person touching it.**

You work for a German hydraulics manufacturer that wants to bid on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. What you need is spread over four websites: the tender portal, a supplier portal with the buyer's specification, your company's ERP and the sales inbox. They behave like real business software, with logins, popups, session timeouts and outdated documents. Your agent reads all of it, applies the bid rules and enters one priced, signed bid in the tender portal.

**What you can use:** Any model through our proxy, your own tools and prompts, and up to four browsers at once. A model does the work in the sandbox: it finds its way through the websites and makes the decisions during the run. No fixed scripts, no crawlers, no copied values, no person helping.

**How you win:** Your bid has to be eligible first. After that, the most accurate bid wins, and between equally accurate bids, the cheaper and faster one. The leaderboard uses the public data. The winners are picked on performance on the private dataset first, then on the public dataset, then on the elegance of the system.

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Challenge id | `rfq` |
| Version | `6` |
| Websites | 4 |
| Test run time limit | 2 hours |
| Scored run time limit | 20 minutes |
| Runs per submission | 1 |
| Public scenario | `public-1` |
| Answer | entered on the `tender-portal` website |
| Largest answer | 65,536 bytes |
| Largest package | 20 MB compressed |

Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq) · Leaderboard: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md) · Getting started: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)

## Quick start for agents

Set the platform URL, install the CLI and sign in once: `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a personal token for this device (`atira login --device` prints a link and a code instead, for a machine without a browser; plain curl uses the [device flow](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in)). Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer`.

```sh
export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh   # the CLI for Node 24; read it first: curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
# or without installing: curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
atira login   # approve in the browser
export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)   # for curl
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites, to run your agent locally
atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq   # one sandbox run on the public dataset, opened live
atira submit ./my-agent --challenge rfq     # review, then the scored run on the public dataset
atira status
```

## How a run works

Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).

1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.

### Develop locally

```sh
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
```

`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.

### Read the run

Inside a test or scored run, with the run token (`$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`) in `RUN_TOKEN`:

```sh
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
```

The response holds `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `url` and `credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `expires_at`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`. Outside a run, `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` returns the brief, logins, answer target and schema for the public websites, without a token.

### In the sandbox

A test run and a scored run start your `run` command with these variables. `setup` runs before, with network but without them, for up to 5 minutes that don't count toward your time.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the platform API; the run is at /v1/runs/current |
| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | this run's token, sent as x-api-key |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | the model proxy with the run token in its path; bring your own provider key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/anthropic |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/openai/v1 |
| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/google |
| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/mistral |
| `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/together/v1 |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | Clef through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/clef, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | Qwen through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/qwen/v1, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
| `CDP_URL` | the sandbox browser (Chrome DevTools Protocol), http://127.0.0.1:9222; with several, browser 1 |
| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: one per browser asked for in agent.json, up to 4 |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started, 1 to 4 |
| `DISPLAY` | the desktop browser 1 runs on, :1 at 1280×800; browser n is on :n |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` | the only way out: the platform and the websites (http://127.0.0.1:3128) |
| `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy` | reached directly, so the browser's CDP stays local (localhost,127.0.0.1) |
| `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` | Node's fetch uses the proxy (1) |

Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. [The run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) has the key and SDK settings for each provider.

## Submitting

A submission is your agent as a gzipped tarball. It is reviewed automatically, then run once in the sandbox on the public dataset, and that score ranks your team. Submit as often as you like, one at a time; your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run.

### agent.json

```json
{
  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
  "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"],
  "models": ["qwen"]
}
```

Put `agent.json` at the root of the tarball, next to your code and its dependency file. Up to 20 MB compressed. `setup` installs dependencies with network access, within 5 minutes that don't count toward your time; `run` is timed and reaches only the platform and the websites. `"browsers": 1–4` (default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts, each on its own screen. `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls; the run waits only for those to warm up (for all of them when it's absent). Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, and Rust with cargo are installed. The [starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal skeleton to start from.

### Upload

```sh
tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
  "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions"
```

Or drop the tarball on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). Upload it as a test run first to watch it work in the sandbox: its browser live, its logs, and a recording afterwards.

### Test run first

The same tarball as a test run: one run in the scored-run sandbox on the public data, with live browser frames, logs and a recording.

```sh
tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
  "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals"
```

### Follow your submissions

```sh
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

Logs of test runs and scored runs, from a cursor (`after`); repeat with the returned `cursor` until `chunks` is empty:

```sh
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=0" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

## Scoring and ranking

Every submission is measured on its run in the sandbox.

- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
- **Cost:** Every model call goes through the proxy and is priced per model. There is no budget: at equal quality, cost × time decides.
- **Time:** Wall-clock time from the start of the run until the answer is accepted. It weighs as much as cost: halving either halves cost × time.

Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

## Fair play

Your agent has to find the answer itself.

- Your system must work the answer out from the websites at run time, with a model doing the navigating and deciding. A coding agent reviews every package; hardcoded answers, fixed scripts and crawlers are rejected.
- Bring your own model key for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, kept as a team secret. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. The sandbox reaches the platform and the websites, nothing else.
- At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up to 4 in agent.json ("browsers"), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The sandbox stops any other browser your agent starts.
- One submission in flight per team. Submit again once it has finished.

Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)

## API for this challenge

| Method | Path | Credential | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` | none | The scouting logins, brief and answer format for the public websites |
| GET | `/v1/runs/current` | run token | The run: brief, logins, answer target and schema |
| POST | `/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` | token | Upload a test run (gzipped tarball) |
| POST | `/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` | token | Submit (gzipped tarball) |
| GET | `/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` | token | Your submissions and their status |
| GET | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/logs?after={cursor}` | token | Logs of a test or scored run |
| POST | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/cancel` | token | Cancel a test or scored run that has not finished |

# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.

Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
get the team disqualified.

## Flagged results

A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
lists flagged results, without a rank.

An orchestrating model reads the brief and directs browsing sub-agents, one browser per website, in parallel. It
decides what to investigate where, follows up on gaps, works out the bid with exact arithmetic helpers, and finally
has a sub-agent enter and sign the bid on the submission website.

from calc import calculate
from llm import Model

ORCHESTRATOR = """You are the lead sales engineer preparing exactly one tender response. You cannot browse yourself:
you direct browsing assistants, one per website, and they report back. You make the decisions.

Approach:
1. Read the brief and its rules closely; they define the one correct answer. Plan which facts you need.
2. Send assistants to the websites with `investigate` — several in one turn run in parallel. Give each a precise
   task: what to find, which exact reference, which details (dates, units, status, validity, senders), and to report
   verbatim. Their first pass should survey their site for everything the rules might need; information may sit on
   any site, so ask each assistant to report anything relevant it sees.
3. Check the reports against the rules. Follow up with targeted investigations for gaps or contradictions (e.g. a
   catalogue group found in the specification must then be searched in the ERP; amendments found in Q&A must be
   applied to the right revision). Do not invent values; a fact you never saw is unknown.
4. Compute with `calculate` (exact decimal arithmetic) — never do arithmetic in your head.
5. Call `submit_bid` with the final answer JSON. It validates the JSON, then an assistant enters and signs it.
   If time is short, submit your best answer: every field scores on its own; leave optional fields out if unknown.

The clock: about {minutes} minutes to investigate. Then you must call `submit_bid` with what you have; entering
and signing the bid takes the rest of the time."""

SCORED_RUN_SECONDS = 20 * 60
# A test run expires hours after it starts and a local run never: those work with a shorter time, so a development
# run reports sooner. A scored run always works with all the time the platform gives it.
TEST_RUN_SECONDS = 10 * 60
# How the working time is spent, as shares of it.
COLLECT_SHARE = 0.65  # investigations end here
SUBMIT_SHARE = 0.70  # from here on the lead must submit
FINISH_SHARE = 0.95  # the bid must be entered and signed by here; the rest is a safety margin


class Orchestrator:
    def __init__(self, task: dict, token: str | None, tabs: dict[str, Tab], model: Model, started: float):
        self.task, self.token, self.tabs, self.model = task, token, tabs, model
        self.credentials = {a["siteId"]: a.get("credentials", {}) for a in task["access"]}
        self.started = started
        now = time.time()
        left = contract.seconds_left(task)
        if left > SCORED_RUN_SECONDS * 1.5:  # not a scored run
            left = TEST_RUN_SECONDS - (now - started)
        self.collect_until = now + left * COLLECT_SHARE
        self.submit_from = now + left * SUBMIT_SHARE
        self.deadline = now + left * FINISH_SHARE
        self.locks = {site: asyncio.Lock() for site in tabs}
        self.submitted = None

    def log(self, text: str):
        print(f"[{time.time() - self.started:6.1f}s] {text}", flush=True)

    def context(self) -> str:
        return (f"# The brief (rules apply exactly)\n{self.task['brief']}\n\n"
                f"# Answer schema\n{json.dumps(self.task['answer_schema'], ensure_ascii=False)}")

    def tools(self) -> list[dict]:
        sites = list(self.tabs)
        return [
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "investigate",
                "description": "Send a browsing assistant to one website with a precise task; returns its report.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "site": {"type": "string", "enum": sites},
                    "task": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["site", "task"]}}},
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "calculate",
                "description": "Exact decimal arithmetic. Python-like expressions with + - * / ( ), and functions "
                               "round_half_up(x, places), ceil(x), floor(x), min, max, sum([..]). "
                               "Several named lines allowed: 'a = 2*3\\nb = a/7\\nround_half_up(b, 2)'. Returns every value.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"expression": {"type": "string"}},
                               "required": ["expression"]}}},
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "submit_bid",
                "description": "Validate the final answer (JSON object per the answer schema) and have an assistant "
                               "enter and sign it on the submission website. Give any form hints you learned.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "answer": {"type": "object"},
                    "hints": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["answer"]}}},
        ]

    async def investigate(self, site: str, task: str) -> str:
        if site not in self.tabs:
            return f"Unknown site {site}; choose one of {', '.join(self.tabs)}"
        async with self.locks[site]:
            if time.time() >= self.collect_until:
                return "No time left to investigate: call submit_bid now with what you have."
            agent = BrowsingAgent(self.model, {site: self.tabs[site]}, self.credentials, task, self.context(),
                                  name=site, deadline=self.collect_until, log=self.log)
            return await agent.run()

    async def submit(self, answer: dict, hints: str) -> str:
        problems = validate(answer, self.task["answer_schema"])
        if problems:
            return "The answer does not match the schema: " + "; ".join(problems)
        submission = self.task["submission"]
        if submission.get("kind") == "api":
            if not self.token:
                self.submitted = answer
                return "Local run: answer recorded, nothing is submitted."
            status, body = contract.submit_answer(self.task, self.token, answer)
            if status == 202:
                self.submitted = answer
            return f"HTTP {status}: {body[:1500]}"
        target = submission.get("siteId")
        sites = {target: self.tabs[target]}
        sites.update({s: t for s, t in self.tabs.items() if s != target})  # e.g. the mailbox for a signing code
        task = ("Enter this bid on the submission website exactly as given and submit it, following the brief's "
                "Submission section step by step (register/express interest if needed, configure every position, "
                "enter numbers in the site's number format, acknowledge documents, get the signing code where the "
                "brief says, review the summary against the answer, confirm). Use each value exactly; do not "
                "recompute. Report the receipt or any validation message verbatim.\n\nANSWER:\n"
                + json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + (f"\n\nHINTS:\n{hints}" if hints else ""))
        agent = BrowsingAgent(self.model, sites, self.credentials, task, self.context(), name="submit",
                              deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=90, log=self.log)
        self.submitted = answer
        return await agent.run()

    async def run(self):
        minutes = round((self.submit_from - time.time()) / 60)
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": ORCHESTRATOR.format(minutes=minutes)},
            {"role": "user", "content": self.context() + "\n\n# Websites\n" + "\n".join(
                f"- {a['siteId']}: {a['url']}" for a in self.task["access"]) + "\n\nBegin."},
        ]
        tools = self.tools()
        while time.time() < self.deadline:
            if time.time() >= self.submit_from and not self.submitted:
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Investigation time is over: call submit_bid now with "
                                 "your best answer. Leave out positions you could not complete."})
            message = await self.model.chat(messages, tools, temperature=0.2)
            calls = message.tool_calls or []
            if message.content:
                self.log(f"[lead] {message.content[:1500]}")
            entry = {"role": "assistant", "content": message.content or ""}
            if calls:
                entry["tool_calls"] = [{"id": c.id, "type": "function",
                                        "function": {"name": c.function.name, "arguments": c.function.arguments}} for c in calls]
            messages.append(entry)
            if not calls:
                if self.submitted:
                    return
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Continue: investigate, calculate, or submit_bid."})
                continue

            async def execute(call):
                try:
                    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
                except ValueError:
                    return "Error: arguments were not valid JSON"
                self.log(f"[lead] {call.function.name} {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False)[:600]}")
                try:
                    if call.function.name == "investigate":
                        return await self.investigate(args["site"], args["task"])
                    if call.function.name == "calculate":
                        return calculate(args["expression"])
                    if call.function.name == "submit_bid":
                        return await self.submit(args["answer"], args.get("hints", ""))
                    return f"Unknown tool {call.function.name}"
                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                    return f"Error: {error}"

            results = await asyncio.gather(*(execute(c) for c in calls))
            for call, result in zip(calls, results):
                self.log(f"[lead] <- {call.function.name}: {result[:3000]}")
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": result})
            if self.submitted and any(c.function.name == "submit_bid" for c in calls):
                return

"""FactsBuilder: facts sent in pieces, in any order, give the same bid as the facts sent at once."""
import random
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal as D

from test_engine_base import core_facts
from test_engine_random import invent

from engine import evaluate
from facts import FactsBuilder, to_dict, update_schema


def pieces(data: dict, rng: random.Random) -> list[dict]:
    """Cut plain facts into random updates: list items spread over updates, materials and revisions split field by
    field (each part keeps the identity), every update in random order."""
    updates = [dict() for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6))]
    for name, value in data.items():
        if not isinstance(value, list):
            rng.choice(updates)[name] = value
            continue
        for item in value:
            parts = [item]
            if name == "materials":
                keys = [k for k in item if k != "material_number"]
                rng.shuffle(keys)
                cut = rng.randint(0, len(keys))
                parts = [{"material_number": item["material_number"], **{k: item[k] for k in keys[:cut]}},
                         {"material_number": item["material_number"], **{k: item[k] for k in keys[cut:]}}]
            elif name == "revisions" and isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("requirements"):
                reqs = list(item["requirements"])
                cut = rng.randint(0, len(reqs))
                parts = [{**item, "requirements": reqs[:cut]}, {"revision": item["revision"], "requirements": reqs[cut:]}]
            for part in parts:
                rng.choice(updates).setdefault(name, []).append(part)
    rng.shuffle(updates)
    return updates


class Builder(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_round_trip_of_core_facts(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add(to_dict(core_facts()))
        self.assertEqual(evaluate(b.facts()).answer, evaluate(core_facts()).answer)

    def test_random_tenders_in_pieces(self):
        for seed in range(0, 300, 3):
            with self.subTest(seed=seed):
                facts = invent(seed).facts
                b = FactsBuilder()
                for update in pieces(to_dict(facts), random.Random(seed)):
                    b.add(update)
                self.assertEqual(evaluate(b.facts()).answer, evaluate(facts).answer)

    def test_material_fields_arrive_in_parts(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add({"materials": [{"material_number": "M-1", "bore_mm": 50, "stock": 7}]})
        b.add({"materials": [{"material_number": "M-1", "stock": 9, "pressure_bar": None}]})
        self.assertEqual(b.data["materials"], [{"material_number": "M-1", "bore_mm": 50, "stock": 9}])

    def test_same_identity_replaces_also_with_other_date_format(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        mail = {"reference": "T-1", "key": "VP-1", "source": {"date": "2030-03-01T09:00:00Z", "sender": "a@b.test"}}
        b.add({"packaging_tariffs": [{**mail, "eur_per_carton": 5}]})
        b.add({"packaging_tariffs": [{**mail, "eur_per_carton": 6,
                                      "source": {"date": "01.03.2030 09:00", "sender": "A@B.test"}}]})
        self.assertEqual([t["eur_per_carton"] for t in b.data["packaging_tariffs"]], [6])

    def test_other_date_is_another_record(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        mail = {"reference": "T-1", "key": "VP-1", "eur_per_carton": 5}
        b.add({"packaging_tariffs": [{**mail, "source": {"date": "2030-03-01"}}]})
        b.add({"packaging_tariffs": [{**mail, "source": {"date": "2030-03-02"}}]})
        self.assertEqual(len(b.data["packaging_tariffs"]), 2)

    def test_bad_update_rejected_whole_and_state_kept(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add({"tender_reference": "T-1", "positions": [{"position": "1", "quantity": 3}]})
        before = b.data
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            b.add({"positions": [{"position": "2", "quantity": 4}], "materials": [{"material_number": "M",
                                                                                    "stock": "viele"}]})
        self.assertIn("Material.stock", str(ctx.exception))
        self.assertIs(b.data, before)
        self.assertEqual(len(b.data["positions"]), 1)

    def test_replace_lists_takes_back_records(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add({"discount_approvals": [{"reference": "T-1-X", "percent": 9}]})
        b.add({"replace_lists": ["discount_approvals"],
               "discount_approvals": [{"reference": "T-1", "percent": 4}]})
        self.assertEqual(b.data["discount_approvals"], [{"reference": "T-1", "percent": 4}])
        b.add({"replace_lists": ["discount_approvals"]})
        self.assertEqual(b.data["discount_approvals"], [])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            b.add({"replace_lists": ["nonsense"]})

    def test_searched_groups_union(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add({"searched_groups": ["G-1"]})
        b.add({"searched_groups": ["g-1", "G-2"]})
        self.assertEqual(b.data["searched_groups"], ["G-1", "G-2"])

    def test_authority_merges(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add({"authority": {"FxRate": "treasury"}})
        b.add({"authority": {"SetupPool": "plant"}})
        self.assertEqual(b.facts.__self__.data["authority"], {"FxRate": "treasury", "SetupPool": "plant"})

    def test_facts_need_reference_and_date(self):
        b = FactsBuilder()
        b.add({"positions": [{"position": "1", "quantity": 1}]})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            b.facts()
        self.assertIn("tender_reference", str(ctx.exception))
        b.add({"tender_reference": "T-1", "scenario_date": "2030-03-15"})
        self.assertEqual(b.facts().positions[0].quantity, D(1))

**What's new in `facts.py`** (nothing existing changed, so Orhun's agent can keep building as it is):
- **`FactsBuilder`** collects the facts over several tool calls, as each report comes in:
  - Each piece is checked straight away. A piece with a bad field is rejected whole, with the field named, and what was collected before stays intact.
  - Re-sending a record with the same identity corrects it rather than duplicating it: the same material number, or the same mail key, date and sender.
  - A material's attributes, stock and price conditions can arrive in separate pieces, and a missing value never wipes out a known one.
  - Records added by mistake can be taken back.
- **`update_schema()`** is the tool schema for one piece.
- **`to_dict()`** turns the facts back into plain JSON, e.g. to log them in a run. Then a test run's lost points can be traced to the facts the lead filled in.

**How I tested it:** 50 of the random tenders are cut into random pieces, sent in random order, and must give exactly the same bid as when sent in one piece. With the field-by-field merging of materials switched off on purpose, 47 of the 50 fail, so the test does catch that kind of bug.

**What Orhun's agent does with it:** two tools instead of one. `add_facts` passes each piece to the builder, and `price_bid` (no parameters) prices the facts collected so far. """A plain-text account of a bid for the run log: what each value was computed from and which records counted.
It reads the facts and the engine's results; it decides nothing itself."""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from decimal import Decimal

from facts import AssignmentKind, Facts, norm_key

from . import resolve
from .money import div, half_up
from .pricing import scale_price, valid_condition

RECORD_LISTS = ("discount_approvals", "condition_groups", "metal_indices", "packaging_tariffs",
                "delivery_commitments", "fx_rates", "setup_pools", "project_bonuses", "end_reserves")


def _money(x: Decimal | None) -> str:
    return "unknown" if x is None else str(half_up(x))


def _src(record) -> str:
    s = record.source
    if s is None:
        return "no source"
    parts = [s.date.isoformat() if s.date else "no date", s.sender or "", s.site, s.document]
    return ", ".join(p for p in parts if p)


def explain(facts: Facts, result) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []
    a = result.answer
    out.append(f"Tender {facts.tender_reference}, scenario date {facts.scenario_date.isoformat()}: "
               f"{a['decision']}, discount {a['discount_percent']} %, total {a['total_net']} EUR")
    out += _discount(facts, result)
    revision = resolve.governing_revision(facts, [])
    if revision:
        how = "marked current" if revision.current else "latest dated, none marked current"
        out.append(f"Specification: revision {revision.revision} ({how})")
    by_id = {norm_key(p.position): p for p in facts.positions}
    pooled: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    for ln in result.lines:
        if ln.material is not None and ln.pieces is not None:
            pooled[norm_key(ln.material.material_number)] += ln.pieces
    for ln in result.lines:
        out += _position(facts, revision, by_id[norm_key(ln.position)], ln, pooled)
    out += _records(facts)
    if result.issues:
        out.append("Issues:")
        out += [f"  - {i}" for i in result.issues]
    return "\n".join(out)


def _discount(facts: Facts, result) -> list[str]:
    approval = resolve.discount_approval(facts, [])
    if approval is None:
        return ["Discount: no approval for this exact reference counts -> 0 %"]
    text = f"Discount: approval {approval.percent} % ({_src(approval)})"
    if approval.min_order_value is not None:
        bases = [ln for ln in result.lines if ln.base is not None and ln.pieces is not None]
        value = half_up(sum((ln.pieces * ln.base for ln in bases), Decimal(0)))
        met = "met" if value >= approval.min_order_value else "NOT met -> 0 %"
        text += f", needs order value >= {approval.min_order_value}, order value {value}: {met}"
    return [text]


def _position(facts: Facts, revision, pos, ln, pooled) -> list[str]:
    out = [f"Position {ln.position}: {resolve.quantity_story(facts, pos)} = {ln.pieces} pieces"]
    req = resolve.requirement(facts, revision, pos.requirement, [])
    if req is None:
        return out + [f"  requirement {pos.requirement}: not found"]
    travel = " (usable travel + 2 x end reserve)" if req.usable_travel else ""
    out.append(f"  requirement {req.requirement}: bore {req.bore_mm}, stroke {req.stroke_mm}{travel}, pressure "
               f"{req.pressure_bar}, mounting {req.mounting}, certification {req.certification or 'none'}, "
               f"group {req.catalogue_group or '-'}")
    group = norm_key(req.catalogue_group)
    others = [m for m in facts.materials if m is not ln.material and (not group or norm_key(m.catalogue_group) == group)]
    rejected = [f"{m.material_number} ({', '.join(resolve.mismatches(m, req)) or ('inactive' if m.active is False else 'status unknown')})"
                for m in others]
    chosen = ln.material.material_number if ln.material else "none"
    out.append(f"  material {chosen}" + (f"; not: {'; '.join(rejected)}" if rejected else ""))
    m = ln.material
    if m is None or ln.pieces is None:
        return out
    cond = valid_condition(m, facts, [])
    if cond is not None:
        per_piece = scale_price(cond, ln.pieces)
        reached = [s.min_quantity for s in cond.scales if s.min_quantity <= ln.pieces]
        fx = f" {cond.currency}, FX key {cond.fx_key}" if norm_key(cond.currency) not in ("", "EUR") else " EUR"
        out.append(f"  price condition {cond.valid_from} .. {cond.valid_to}{fx}, per {cond.price_unit} pieces, scale "
                   f"from {max(reached) if reached else '-'} -> {per_piece} per piece; base {_money(ln.base)} EUR")
    n = ln.pieces or 1
    index = f" ({m.surcharge_mass_kg} kg x index {m.metal_index})" if m.metal_index else ""
    out.append(f"  per piece before discount: base {_money(ln.base)}, mass surcharge {_money(ln.mass_surcharge)}"
               f"{index}; whole position: setup {_money(ln.setup)}, pool {_money(ln.pool)}, packaging "
               f"{_money(ln.packaging)}, bonus {_money(ln.bonus)} (per piece "
               f"{_money(div(ln.packaging, n)) if ln.packaging is not None else 'unknown'} packaging)")
    group_key = resolve.assignment(facts, ln.position, AssignmentKind.CONDITION_GROUP)
    out.append(f"  discount applies to: {ln.scope.value}"
               + (f" (Konditionsgruppe {group_key.key})" if group_key else " (default, no Konditionsgruppe)")
               + f"; unit price {_money(ln.unit_price)}")
    commit = resolve.assignment(facts, ln.position, AssignmentKind.DELIVERY)
    out.append(f"  lead time {ln.lead_weeks} weeks: stock {m.stock}, pooled demand "
               f"{pooled[norm_key(m.material_number)]}, stock {m.stock_lead_weeks} / production "
               f"{m.production_lead_weeks} weeks" + (f", commitment key {commit.key}" if commit else ""))
    return out


def _records(facts: Facts) -> list[str]:
    out = ["Mail records:"]
    for name in RECORD_LISTS:
        records = getattr(facts, name)
        if not records:
            continue
        if name == "discount_approvals":
            keyfn = (lambda r: "approval")
        elif name == "end_reserves":
            keyfn = (lambda r: f"{norm_key(r.key)} / {norm_key(r.revision)}")
        else:
            keyfn = (lambda r: norm_key(r.key))
        used = ({"approval": resolve.discount_approval(facts, [])} if name == "discount_approvals"

I've pushed the branch and opened the PR: https://github.com/OrhunMahir/ehl-day-by-day/pull/2. It merges without conflicts and only touches your files and your log, so you can merge it yourself, again with "Create a merge commit". All 105 engine tests pass.

The push contains three things:

1. **Facts in pieces (`FactsBuilder`):** the lead model can add facts tool call by tool call, as the reports come in. A bad piece is rejected on its own, and what was already collected stays.
2. **Explanation for the run log (`result.explain()`):** for each position, it says where the quantity, material, price and lead time came from. For each mail key, it says which record counted and why the others were ignored (older, other tender, dated after the scenario date, wrong sender). When a test run loses points on a field, we can look up why in the log.
3. **Guide for filling in the facts (`facts.FILLING_GUIDE`):** a text for the lead model's prompt saying which fact goes in which field, with the traps from the rules and no values from the sites. A test fails if the guide names a field that doesn't exist.

Writing the guide also turned up one gap, now fixed: if the sales director's address isn't filled in, discount approvals from any sender count, including the sales team's own request mail. The engine now flags that in its issues.

- put `FILLING_GUIDE` into the lead's prompt;

- print `result.explain()` into the run log after each pricing.

The thorough check is done, and it found and fixed four real problems. All 107 engine tests pass on Python 3.12 (the sandbox version) as well as locally. The fixes are committed locally, not pushed yet.

**What passed without problems**
- Everything works on Python 3.12, the version the sandbox runs.
- The linter is clean.
- The package contains `facts.py` and the whole `engine/`.
- No value from the public sites appears in any file of the package; I checked 115 values from the scouting notes.
- The full test suite shows only the 3 known failures in Orhun's `test_kit.py`.

**What I found and fixed**
1. **Bad facts could break the bid.** If the lead model sent a position twice, an empty position number, a negative quantity or price, or a discount above 100 %, the engine either crashed or produced an answer the form would reject. That costs time in the run, or the whole bid. Now bad input counts as unknown and is listed in the issues, and the answer stays valid. 3,400 deliberately damaged tenders: no crash, every answer passes the schema.
2. **No-bid after a misreading.** One misread attribute is enough to turn a good bid into a no-bid, which loses almost all the points. The engine can't tell the two apart, but it now names the nearest candidates when it decides no-bid, e.g. "closest: M-X: pressure 170 (required 160)". The lead model can re-check exactly that value once. This is in your push log for Orhun.
3. **Collecting facts was far too slow.** A large tender took 235 seconds for 282 pieces; it now takes 2.8 seconds with the same result.
4. **Small fixes:** an unused import, overlong lines and a weak spot in a test, all from the linter.

**Speed with a large tender** (100 positions, 412 materials, 3,872 mail records): calculating takes 1.5 seconds and the explanation 0.9 seconds.

content.text:
Yes, I have access. As a team member I can see all test runs through the CLI and the API, including the points per field (I saved how to do this in memory). Both scored runs are from before the engine was merged, so they show the baseline.

**Overview:** 10 test runs. 2 are running right now, started at 14:00 UTC, probably with the latest changes.

| Result | Runs |
|---|---|
| Finished with an answer | 2: quality **18.3** (16 min, $0.14) and **5** (13 min, $0.17) |
| No answer submitted, quality 0 | 5: four ran out the full 20 minutes, one stopped after 9 |
| Cancelled | 1 (Orhun, the first run, 37 min) |

**What the points show:**
1. **The biggest problem is not submitting at all.** Five of eight runs ended without an answer, which means quality 0 and not eligible. That's Orhun's area (the deadline guard). His newest commit on `stream-o` ("forced submission, resubmit until accepted") targets exactly that.
2. **In the best run, the order-level points are right.** Decision, tender reference and discount: 15 points.
3. **The positions bring almost nothing.** The best run got 3.25 out of a possible 65 or so. **The material is wrong in all 5 positions in both runs.** That is the most expensive field (20 % per position), and every price builds on it. Quantities were right only once.

**What this means for us:** the engine computes correctly, but only from correct facts. With the wrong material, every price is wrong too. Material selection fails before the engine is ever involved: the current revision, the Q&A amendments, usable travel plus reserves, and the ERP candidates.

That makes the checklist of missing facts (idea 1 from earlier) the most useful next step. The engine would tell the lead model exactly: "for position 3, the ERP search for Kataloggruppe G hasn't been done", "end reserve for key E in revision R is missing", "no candidate matches; re-check pressure". I'll keep the other ideas in mind as you asked.

Should I start on the checklist, or would you rather wait for the two running test runs first? They should be finished within about 20 minutes.
yes, start

I'll build it as a separate module, `engine/needs.py`, like the explanation: it reads the facts and the engine's results and decides nothing itself. Each entry says what is missing, where to look (by the site's role, not its name, since the final run's sites are named differently), for which positions, and under which rule. There are two kinds:
- **find:** a fact is missing, so the bid can't be complete.
- **verify:** a value is assumed or suspicious (e.g. setup fee taken as 0, a no-bid that hinges on one attribute).

When there are no more "find" entries, the lead model knows it can submit.

"""The checklist of what is still missing (engine/needs.py): every gap the engine meets is named."""
import copy
import random
import unittest
from dataclasses import replace

from test_engine_base import core_facts
from test_engine_random import invent
from test_engine_robust import damage

from engine import evaluate


def unexplained(result) -> list[str]:
    """Positions left out or incompletely priced for which no "find" entry names the position or the whole bid."""
    needs = [n for n in result.needed() if n["kind"] == "find"]
    covered = {p for n in needs for p in n.get("positions", [])}
    global_need = any(not n.get("positions") for n in needs)
    return [p for p in result.omitted + result.incomplete if p not in covered and not global_need]


REMOVALS = {
    "fx rate": lambda f: f.fx_rates.clear(),
    "metal index": lambda f: f.metal_indices.clear(),
    "packaging tariff": lambda f: f.packaging_tariffs.clear(),
    "setup pool": lambda f: f.setup_pools.clear(),
    "project bonus": lambda f: f.project_bonuses.clear(),
    "condition group rule": lambda f: f.condition_groups.clear(),
    "delivery commitment": lambda f: f.delivery_commitments.clear(),
    "end reserve": lambda f: f.end_reserves.clear(),
    "price conditions": lambda f: [setattr(m, "conditions", []) for m in f.materials],
    "stock": lambda f: [setattr(m, "stock", None) for m in f.materials],
    "carton size": lambda f: [setattr(m, "pieces_per_carton", None) for m in f.materials],
    "allocation mass": lambda f: [setattr(m, "allocation_mass_kg", None) for m in f.materials],
    "surcharge mass": lambda f: [setattr(m, "surcharge_mass_kg", None) for m in f.materials],
    "materials": lambda f: (f.materials.clear(), f.searched_groups.clear()),
    "pieces per set": lambda f: [setattr(r, "pieces_per_set", None) for v in f.revisions for r in v.requirements],
    "current mark": lambda f: [setattr(v, "current", None) for v in f.revisions],
    "revisions": lambda f: f.revisions.clear(),
}


class Needs(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_complete_facts_need_nothing(self):
        result = evaluate(core_facts())
        self.assertTrue(result.complete)
        self.assertEqual([n for n in result.needed() if n["kind"] == "find"], [])

    def test_each_kind_of_missing_fact_is_named(self):
        for name, remove in REMOVALS.items():
            for seed in range(0, 300, 15):
                with self.subTest(removed=name, seed=seed):
                    facts = copy.deepcopy(invent(seed).facts)
                    remove(facts)
                    result = evaluate(facts)
                    self.assertEqual(unexplained(result), [])
                    if result.omitted or result.incomplete:
                        self.assertFalse(result.complete)

    def test_damaged_facts_gaps_are_named(self):
        for seed in range(200):
            with self.subTest(seed=seed):
                result = evaluate(damage(copy.deepcopy(invent(seed % 300).facts), random.Random(seed)))
                self.assertEqual(unexplained(result), [], result.issues)

    def test_examples(self):
        f = core_facts()
        f.director_address = ""
        f.materials = [m for m in f.materials if m.catalogue_group != "G-B"]
        f.materials[0] = replace(f.materials[0], conditions=[])
        needs = {n["what"]: n for n in evaluate(f).needed()}
        self.assertIn("director_address: the sales director's mail address", needs)
        search = next(n for w, n in needs.items() if w.startswith("search Kataloggruppe G-B"))
        self.assertEqual((search["kind"], search["site"], search["positions"], search["rule"]), ("find", "ERP", ["2"], 10))
        self.assertTrue(any(w.startswith("price conditions of M-A1") for w in needs))

    def test_no_bid_asks_for_a_recheck(self):
        f = core_facts()
        f.materials = [m for m in f.materials if m.material_number != "M-B1"]
        f.searched_groups = ["G-B"]
        result = evaluate(f)
        self.assertEqual(result.answer["decision"], "no_bid")
        self.assertTrue(any(n["kind"] == "verify" and "no_bid" in n["what"] for n in result.needed()))


if __name__ == "__main__":

The checklist is done and committed locally (not pushed, so it can go up together with the next change). All 112 engine tests pass on Python 3.12 and 3.14.

**What it does:** after every pricing, `result.needed()` returns a list of what's still missing. Each entry says:
- whether something is missing (**find**) or should be checked again (**verify**);
- where to look, by the site's role (brief, tender portal, specification, ERP, mailbox), since the sites have other names in the final run;
- what exactly to read, for which positions, and under which rule.

Example: `find · ERP · "search Kataloggruppe G-B and record every candidate (also inactive ones and near misses)" · positions ["2"] · rule 10`. Outstanding ERP searches come first, because nothing else for that position can be checked without them. `result.complete` is true when nothing is left to find; that's the lead model's signal to stop investigating and submit.

**How I made sure it's reliable:** the requirement is that every gap gets named. For each position the engine leaves out or can't fully price, there must be at least one "find" entry for it.
- I removed each of 17 kinds of facts in turn (FX rate, metal index, stock, price conditions, end reserve, pieces per set, …) across many random tenders.
- I also damaged 3,000 tenders at random, twice each.

In the end no gap went unnamed. Along the way the tests found five kinds the checklist missed at first. One example: a position in EUR can't be priced completely because it shares a project bonus with a USD position whose FX rate is missing. They're all named now. All 300 complete random tenders are marked `complete`.

**Faster as a side effect:** the checklist was too slow at first (3.3 s on 100 positions). With cached text normalisation, the engine went from 1.5 s to 0.4 s, the checklist takes 0.8 s, and the explanation 0.2 s.

**For Orhun** (in your push log): return `needed()` with every `price_bid` result, have the lead work through the "find" entries in order, and submit as soon as `complete` is true or time runs out.

**Test runs:** two new runs are going right now, and their packages are 34 files instead of 27, so the engine is probably already included. A third (from 14:00) was cancelled. Once one finishes, I'll look at its points per field (again points only, never values).

   334	    def read_file(self, name: str, offset: int = 0) -> str:

   343	    async def collect_pages(self, aid: str, max_pages: int = 10) -> str:
   344	        """Follows a paging control the model chose ("next page", "load more") until it disappears or `max_pages`
   345	        views are collected, and joins them. The control is found again on each new view by its visible text."""
   346	        first = await self.observe()
   347	        match = re.search(r"^\[" + re.escape(aid.strip().strip("[]")) + r"\] (link|button|clickable) \"([^\"]*)\"", self.last_text, re.M)
   348	        if not match or not match.group(2).strip():
   349	            return f"Element {aid} is not a link or button with text on this page.\n" + first
   350	        kind, label = match.group(1), match.group(2)
   351	        views, seen = [self.last_text], set(self.last_text.splitlines())
   352	        urls = [self.page.url]

   356	            await self.click(current)

   372	        if len(joined) > MAX_OBSERVATION:
   373	            body += f"\n... (continues: read_more with offset={MAX_OBSERVATION})"
   374	        return note + body

1	"""A browsing sub-agent: a model works one or more websites through numbered page views until it can report.
     2	
     3	The model picks every navigation target, search and document. Code only executes the action it chose, renders the
     4	page as text, and keeps the conversation small: older page views are dropped once newer ones exist, while the
     5	facts the model saved with `note` stay.
     6	"""
     7	import asyncio
     8	import json
     9	import time

    11	from browser import Tab, origin

    13	TOOLS = [

    70	SYSTEM = """You are a careful sales-engineering assistant operating real business websites through a text view of the browser.

    77	Working rules:

    79	  unrelated offers), decoy buttons that do nothing, error pages that work on a retry, session timeouts that send you

   111	async def _shows_sign_in(tab: Tab) -> bool:

   131	class BrowsingAgent:
   132	    def __init__(self, model, tabs: dict[str, Tab], credentials: dict[str, dict], task: str, context: str,
   133	                 name: str, deadline: float, max_steps: int = 60, log=print):
   134	        self.model, self.tabs, self.credentials = model, tabs, credentials
   135	        self.task, self.context, self.name = task, context, name

        self.credentials = {a["siteId"]: a.get("credentials", {}) for a in task["access"]}

        # Every run works with the length of a scored run: a test run expires much later, a local run never.
        left = min(contract.seconds_left(task), SCORED_RUN_SECONDS - (now - started))

        self.facts_data: dict = {}  # the facts JSON as the lead has built it up so far
        self.priced: engine.BidResult | None = None  # what the bid engine made of the latest facts
        self.price_failures = 0

        self.sent_without_lead = False

    def log(self, text: str):
        print(f"[{time.time() - self.started:6.1f}s] {text}", flush=True)

    def context(self) -> str:
        return (f"# The brief (rules apply exactly)\n{self.task['brief']}\n\n"

    async def investigate(self, site: str, task: str) -> str:
        if site not in self.tabs:

            if time.time() >= self.collect_until:
                return "No time left to investigate: call submit_bid now with what you have."
            until = min(self.collect_until, time.time() + INVESTIGATION_SECONDS)
            agent = BrowsingAgent(self.worker_model, {site: self.tabs[site]}, self.credentials, f"{task}\n\n{PROVENANCE}",
                                  self.context(), name=site, deadline=until, log=self.log)
            try:
                return await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=until - time.time() + INVESTIGATION_GRACE_SECONDS)

    def price(self, data) -> str:
        if not isinstance(data, dict):

    def without_hasty_no_bid(self, collected: facts.Facts, result: engine.BidResult) -> engine.BidResult:
        """A "no bid" is final only when the engine has nothing else to report and every position without a
        material had its catalogue group searched on purpose. While facts are still missing, the positions without
        a material are left out instead and the others are bid."""
        if result.answer.get("decision") != "no_bid":
            return result
        unresolved = [line.position for line in result.lines if line.material is None]
        searched = {facts.norm_key(group) for group in collected.searched_groups}

        def conclusive(position: facts.TenderPosition) -> bool:
            groups = {facts.norm_key(requirement.catalogue_group)
                      for revision in collected.revisions for requirement in revision.requirements
                      if facts.norm_key(requirement.requirement) == facts.norm_key(position.requirement)}
            return bool(groups) and groups <= searched

        # the engine's own remarks about the unmatched positions do not count as open questions
        open_questions = [issue for issue in result.issues if "no active material matches" not in issue]
        if not open_questions and all(conclusive(p) for p in collected.positions if p.position in unresolved):
            return result
        kept = [position for position in collected.positions if position.position not in unresolved]
        partial = engine.evaluate(dataclasses.replace(collected, positions=kept))
        note = ("no bid was not taken as final: facts are missing or a catalogue group was not searched completely; "
                "position(s) " + ", ".join(unresolved) + " are left out instead")
        return dataclasses.replace(partial, issues=[*result.issues, note], omitted=[*partial.omitted, *unresolved])

                "enter numbers in the site's number format, acknowledge documents, get the signing code where the "
                "brief says, review the summary against the answer, confirm). Use each value exactly; do not "

    """The answer object plus what could not be decided (`issues`) and the per-position working (`lines`)."""
    issues: list[str] = []
    revision = resolve.governing_revision(facts, issues)
    positions = _usable_positions(facts, issues)

    lines: list[Line] = []
    no_match: list[str] = []
    for pos in positions:

        line.pieces = resolve.final_pieces(facts, pos, req, issues)
        if line.pieces is not None and line.pieces < 0:
            issues.append(f"position {pos.position}: negative quantity {line.pieces}, treated as unknown")
            line.pieces = None
        if req is not None and resolve.requirement_complete(req):
            line.material = resolve.select_material(facts, req, pos.position, issues)
            if line.material is None and resolve.searched(facts, req):
                no_match.append(pos.position)
                issues.append(f"position {pos.position}: no active material matches requirement {req.requirement}; "
                              f"closest: {resolve.closest(facts, req)}. Re-check these values before a no_bid.")
            elif line.material is None:
                issues.append(f"position {pos.position}: Kataloggruppe {req.catalogue_group or '(none)'} not "
                              "searched in the ERP yet, material unknown")
        elif req is not None:
            issues.append(f"position {pos.position}: requirement incomplete, material not selected")
        lines.append(line)

    if no_match:
        issues.append(f"no active material matches position(s) {', '.join(no_match)}: no bid (rule 3)")
        percent = _valid_percent(approval.percent, issues) if approval and approval.min_order_value is None else ZERO
        answer = _answer(facts, "no_bid", percent, [], ZERO)
        return BidResult(answer, _dedupe(issues), lines, [], [], facts)

    priced = [ln for ln in lines if ln.material is not None and ln.pieces is not None]
    for ln in priced:
        ln.base = base_unit_price(ln.material, ln.pieces, facts, issues)
    percent = _discount(facts, approval, priced, issues)
    _surcharges(facts, priced, issues)
    _setup_pools(facts, priced, issues)
    _packaging(facts, priced, issues)
    _bonus(facts, priced, issues)
    _scopes(facts, priced, issues)
    _lead_times(facts, priced, issues)

    out, incomplete, omitted, total = [], [], list(_dropped_ids(facts, positions)), ZERO
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.material is None or ln.pieces is None:
            issues.append(f"position {ln.position}: left out (material or quantity unknown)")
            omitted.append(ln.position)
            continue
        number = (ln.material.material_number or "").strip()
        if not number or len(number) > 50:
            issues.append(f"position {ln.position}: material number {number!r} is not usable, left out")
            omitted.append(ln.position)

        ln.unit_price = _unit_price(ln, percent)
        if ln.unit_price is not None and ln.unit_price < 0:

        if ln.unit_price is None:

        total += ln.pieces * unit_price
        out.append(_position(ln, unit_price, issues))
    answer = _answer(facts, "bid", percent, out, half_up(total))
    return BidResult(answer, _dedupe(issues), lines, incomplete, omitted, facts)

I reviewed every file in the package on `main`, plus Orhun's integration on `stream-o`. I fixed what I found in your files, and wrote up the findings in the other streams' files for Julien and Orhun without touching their files. Everything is pushed to `stream-i`. 116 engine tests pass on Python 3.12 and 3.14, and the heavy check over 3,000 damaged tenders found no crash, no invalid answer and no unnamed gap.

**Fixed in your files**
1. **False no-bid without a Kataloggruppe:** if the lead didn't record a requirement's Kataloggruppe, the engine could decide no-bid, which loses almost all points. Now that's a "find" entry.
2. **Discount dropped too early:** with a minimum order value, positions still missing made the order value too low, and the discount fell silently to 0 % (all unit prices wrong). Now it's flagged and checked again once everything is priced.
3. **Invisible characters in the source:** `facts.py` contained raw zero-width and writing-direction characters. Linters flag those as possibly obfuscated code, and Atira's AI reviewer reads the package. They're now visible escape sequences.
4. **Small things:** certification compared with and without spaces, a choice among matching materials that no longer depends on input order, and one dead function and one unused parameter removed.

**Findings for Orhun** (most important first):
- **High: facts get lost.** His `price_bid` replaces whole lists. If the lead sends only new materials in a later call, the earlier ones are gone. `FactsBuilder` solves exactly that.
- **High: a real no-bid gets turned into a partial bid.** His protection against hasty no-bids counts every issue as an open question, including frequent harmless ones like "sender unknown". In a scenario where no-bid is the right answer, a partial bid would still go out, which loses the 75 points for the decision. It should look at the checklist's "find" entries instead.
- **Medium:** `main` still has the old model client, which can fall back to providers' public addresses (a fair-play risk) and allows 600 seconds per call. Both are fixed on his branch, just not merged yet. Until then, a submission from `main` still carries those problems.

**Findings for Julien:**
- **Medium:** `observe.js` has the same invisible characters in its source as my file had.
- **Medium:** the page view shows the contents of password fields, so the login password or a TAN ends up in the prompt and the run log.
- **Medium:** `observe.js` is read without UTF-8 encoding, which fails on Windows.
- **Low:** stray `</script>` tags cut off the rest of a page's text, `fetch_file` loads HTML pages twice, and a note sent in the same turn after `finish` is lost.

All findings with details are in your push log. Tell Julien and Orhun there's something there for them, especially the two high ones for Orhun.

Should I open a PR for the checklist and these fixes into `main`? Orhun will need the checklist for his next integration step.

PR #6 is open and mergeable: https://github.com/OrhunMahir/ehl-day-by-day/pull/6. Like the earlier ones it only touches your files, so you can merge it yourself with "Create a merge commit".

**Findings outside both their streams:** there are none. Every finding sits either in Julien's files or in Orhun's, so there was nothing I could fix on their behalf.

Here are the two prompts. Each colleague can paste theirs into their coding agent as is.

---

**For Julien**

> Written for: Julien's coding agent, working in stream J.

```text
Stream I (Ivan) reviewed the package and found issues in stream J's files. Fix them on stream-j (git switch
stream-j, git pull, git merge origin/main first). Edit only stream J's files (browser.py, observe.js, browsing.py,
browsers.py, tests/test_browser*). Details are also in docs/log/ivan.md, latest entry.

1. observe.js, the `clean` function (around line 11): the regex contains raw invisible characters (zero-width
   spaces and the left-to-right/right-to-left marks U+200E/U+200F). Raw direction marks in source are what linters
   and code reviewers flag as obfuscated code, and Atira's AI reviewer reads every package. Write the character
   class with escapes: /[\u200b-\u200f\u2060\ufeff\u00ad]/g. Then check the whole package for raw invisible
   characters (a short Python loop over the files looking for code points 0x200B-0x200F, 0x2060, 0xFEFF, 0xAD,
   0x202A-0x202E, 0x2066-0x2069) and escape any you find in your files.
2. browser.py line 12: OBSERVE_JS is read with read_text() without encoding; on Windows that decodes as cp1252
   and fails. Use read_text(encoding="utf-8").
3. observe.js, `describe` for INPUT: a password input prints its value (value="..."), so a filled login password
   or a TAN typed into a password-type field goes into the model's prompt and the run log. For type=password,
   show only whether it is filled (e.g. value=<filled>/<empty>).
4. browser.py `_HtmlText.handle_endtag`: a stray </script> or </style> makes `skip` negative, and then all later
   text is dropped (the check is `if not self.skip`). Clamp it: self.skip = max(0, self.skip - 1).
5. browser.py `fetch_file`: for an HTML URL the page is fetched once with fetch() and then loaded again in a
   scratch tab, so a GET with side effects (e.g. a logout or cancel link) runs twice. Render the HTML already
   fetched (e.g. set it as the scratch page's content with the URL as base) instead of loading the URL a second
   time, or at least skip the first fetch for HTML.
6. browsing.py `run`: when the model sends several tool calls in one turn and `finish` comes before a `note`, the
   function returns at `finish` and the later note is lost. Run all non-finish calls of the turn first, then
   handle finish.
7. browsing.py `_shows_sign_in`: any visible password field counts as an expired session, so a password-type TAN
   or code field on a normal page triggers an automatic re-login and a jump back to the previous URL. Only treat
   it as a sign-in page if the form also has a user-name field, or the URL looks like a sign-in page
   (_looks_like_sign_in_url), or the page was not a password page before the action.

Add a test for 3, 4 and 6 in tests/test_browser*.py with invented pages only. Run
`uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` in agent/ (the engine tests must stay green), add a push log entry
to docs/log/julien.md, commit with "J: ..." and push to stream-j.
```

---

**For Orhun**

> Written for: Orhun's coding agent, working in stream O. (I wrote it in English like the code; translate if he prefers.)

```text
Stream I (Ivan) reviewed the package and the engine integration on stream-o and found issues in stream O's files.
First `git merge origin/main` on stream-o: main now has stream I's PR #6 (or merge it when it is merged) with
`result.needed()` and `result.complete`. Edit only stream O's files. Details are also in docs/log/ivan.md, latest
entry.

1. HIGH, agent.py `Orchestrator.price`: the facts are merged by top-level field
   (`{**self.facts_data, **data}`), so a later price_bid that sends only new `materials` (or any other list)
   replaces the whole list and the earlier items are lost; the engine then reports those materials as missing or
   a Kataloggruppe as not searched. Keep a `facts.FactsBuilder` on the Orchestrator instead: `builder.add(data)`
   merges list items by identity (same material number, same mail key + date + sender, ...), merges materials and
   revisions field by field, validates only the update and rejects a bad one whole with the field named (return
   that message to the model). Then `engine.evaluate(builder.facts())`. Use `facts.update_schema()` as the tool's
   parameter schema, so every field is optional and `replace_lists` lets the lead take back wrong records. Log
   `builder.data` instead of `merged`.
2. HIGH, agent.py `without_hasty_no_bid`: every issue other than "no active material matches" counts as an open
   question. Issues like "sender unknown" or "two records with the same date" are common, so in a scenario whose
   correct answer is no_bid the agent would still send a partial bid, and the no_bid decision is worth 75 points.
   The engine itself already refuses a no_bid unless the unmatched requirement's Kataloggruppe was searched. Base
   the check on the checklist instead: keep the no_bid when `result.needed()` has no entry with kind "find" for
   the unmatched positions (or none at all); before submitting a no_bid, have the lead re-check once the values
   the issue names after "closest:".
3. agent.py `price`: return `result.needed()` and `result.complete` with every price_bid result (next to answer,
   issues, incomplete, omitted). In the lead prompt: work through the "find" entries in order (each names the site
   by role, what to read, the rule and the positions; turn them into investigate tasks); "verify" entries are
   checks, not blockers; when `complete` is true, or the time is up, submit.
4. MEDIUM: main still has the old llm.py (fallbacks to the providers' public addresses, a 600 s call timeout);
   stream-o already fixes both. Merge stream-o into main before the next `atira submit`, so a submission never
   carries the old client.
5. LOW, run.py `load_run`: a 200 response whose body is not JSON raises from json.loads instead of being retried;
   treat a JSONDecodeError like a failed attempt.

Run `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` in agent/ (the engine tests must stay green), then one local
run with the scouting logins and one sandbox test run; write the points per field (points only, no values) into
docs/log/orhun.md, commit with "O: ..." and push to stream-o.
```

---

One note for Orhun: point 4 matters before the next `atira submit`. Every submission comes from `main`, and `main` still has the old model client until his branch is merged.

`main` is in good shape, and all review findings are fixed. But the test runs show the agent still loses almost all position points, and the cause is time, not code errors.

**State of `main`**
- All 9 PRs are merged (2 from you, 5 from Julien, 2 from Orhun), and every stream branch is at the state of `main`.
- All 180 tests pass, including Julien's browser tests and Orhun's former `test_kit` failures, and even without the Windows UTF-8 workaround.
- **Julien fixed all 7 points:**
  - invisible characters written as escapes; a scan of the whole package finds none anymore;
  - UTF-8 when reading `observe.js`;
  - password fields show only "filled" or "empty";
  - the HTML parser survives a stray closing tag;
  - pages are loaded only once;
  - `finish` comes last in a turn, so notes sent with it are kept;
  - better detection of an expired session.
- **Orhun fixed all 5 points:**
  - the lead model now collects facts with `FactsBuilder` (`add_facts`);
  - the no-bid check is based on the checklist;
  - `needed` and `complete` reach the lead model;
  - the model client goes through the proxy only, with a 240-second limit;
  - `run.py` retries a reply that isn't JSON.

**Latest test runs** (points only, no values):

| Run (UTC) | Quality | Positions answered |
|---|---|---|
| 14:17 (2 runs) | 10 / 10 | 0 of 5 |
| 14:35 | 15.2 | 1 of 5, with the right material for the first time |
| 14:48 / 14:51 | 10 / 10 | 0 of 5 |
| 15:10 (2 runs) | still running | – |

The 10 points are the decision and the tender reference. The discount was missed every time.

**Why, from the 14:51 run log** (I only evaluated times and counts):
- **The tender and specification facts are complete:** 5 positions, Q&A, withdrawal, 3 revisions with the current mark, all requirement fields.
- **ERP and mailbox delivered nothing:** 0 materials and 0 mail records in the facts. So the engine had to leave every position out, and the discount stays at 0 % with no approval.
- **The reason is the time plan.** The first ERP sub-agent worked from 55 s to 245 s, then hit its time limit before it was done; it also had to search 5 Kataloggruppen and open 3 transactions per candidate. The mailbox sub-agent had two stalled model calls. At 511 s the lead model sent six more ERP and mailbox tasks, but they all stopped at **512 s, one second later**, because the investigation window was already closed. The rest of the time went to the submission (814–940 s).
- **The lead model recorded facts only once** (`add_facts` 1×), against 11 investigations.

**What the team should look at.** These belong to Orhun and Julien, not your stream:
- **Orhun, time plan:** don't send investigations that start after the window has closed. Give the ERP more time in the first round, or have it work on several Kataloggruppen in parallel tabs; his PR #9 enables that, but at 511 s there was no time left for it. After every report, convert the facts with `add_facts` right away instead of waiting until the end.
- **Julien, ERP sub-agent:** 39 steps in 190 seconds isn't enough for 5 groups with 3 transactions per candidate. The task could be split per Kataloggruppe.

The engine itself isn't the bottleneck right now: it gets too few facts. Should I write these points up as a short message for Orhun and Julien, or wait for the two runs that are going right now? They started at 15:10 with Orhun's latest changes, so they'll show whether the timing problem has already improved.

One caution from my side: while evaluating the log, two log lines containing the site addresses and a partly masked username of an already expired run got printed in this session. The addresses are public, and the run logins are invalid after the run, so practically nothing is exposed. I'll still mask more strictly in future.

def t_of(l):
